article_title: Investigation of Conceptual Change about Double-Slit Interference in Secondary School Physics
citation: Mustafa Sabri Kocakulah, Mehmet Kural. (2010). Investigation of conceptual change about double-slit interference in secondary school physics. International Journal of Environmental & Science Education. http://www.ijese.com/
title: Yip's three-source taxonomy of students' science misconceptions
description: The article adopts Yip's (1998) classification of students' misconceptions in science after teaching by the nature and origin of their sources into three broad groups: informal ideas generated through life experiences that students bring to class; misconceptions developed during teaching, defined as "incomplete or improper views" arising from missing prerequisite knowledge; and instructional misconceptions originating from teachers and textbooks. The article uses this taxonomy to frame why student ideas resist instruction and how teaching should be designed to remedy them. It states that "Yip (1998) categorizes students‟ misconceptions in science after teaching according to the nature and sources of origin into three broad grou ps."
requirements: Identification of misconceptions and monitoring the development of informal views are needed to construct effective teaching strategies that remedy them
constraints: The taxonomy applies to misconceptions present after teaching, categorized by the nature and sources of their origin
target_learners: science students in secondary and university education
target_learning_goals: replacing misconceptions with scientific conceptions in physics topics such as the wave model of light
examples: The article cites Kousathana, Demerouti and Tsaparlis (2005) terming the teacher- and textbook-origin category instructional misconceptions and suggesting inclusion of history of science in instruction
key_sources: Mustafa Sabri Kocakulah, Mehmet Kural. (2010). Investigation of conceptual change about double-slit interference in secondary school physics. International Journal of Environmental & Science Education. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ908941

article_title: Inclusive Mobile Learning: How Technology-Enabled Language Choice Supports Multilingual Students
citation: Phenyo Phemelo Moletsane, Michael W. Asher, Christine Kwon, Paulo F. Carvalho, and Amy Ogan. (2026). Inclusive Mobile Learning: How Technology-Enabled Language Choice Supports Multilingual Students. Proceedings of the 2026 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems (CHI '26). https://doi.org/10.1145/3772318.3791139
title: Yiya Solutions radio-and-phone STEM course platform
description: Yiya Solutions is the offline, remote learning platform studied: "an offline, remote learning platform designed to bring interactive hands-on 15-week STEM education to participants in rural Uganda". It relies on basic keypad phones and radios; learners receive Robocall and SMS alerts, listen to ~30-minute radio broadcasts, and answer multiple-choice practice questions and weekly assessments in real time via free USSD menus. The 15-week curriculum follows nine Engineering Design Process steps culminating in a hands-on product (a solar-powered food dehydrator), a 16-question final exam, and a community exhibition.
requirements: Learners need access to a basic keypad phone and radio broadcasts; USSD restricts interaction to multiple-choice formats due to character limits
constraints: Electricity cuts can disrupt phone use, device sharing can reduce engagement, and radio instruction is linear and broadcast-dependent, limiting real-time interaction
target_learners: Out-of-school and in-school rural learners in Northern Uganda
target_learning_goals: Practical STEM and engineering problem-solving skills through building a solar-powered food dehydrator
examples: Learners entered prize codes read aloud during broadcasts to unlock practice questions, and active participants could receive materials kits for their final products
